programme: MED1, NONO, and NR2C1 converge on a nuclear hormone-receptor coactivation module: MED1 (Mediator) and NONO both regulate AR/PGR/steroid-linked genes (their target lists include AR, PGR, CYP17A1, KLK3, VDR, RARB), while NR2C1 (TR2) is itself an orphan nuclear receptor whose targets include ESR1, RARB, and KLK3 — together forming a coactivator/receptor layer that tunes steroid-hormone-responsive transcription.
role_in_a: In breast cancer this axis sets the output of the estrogen/androgen/progesterone receptor programme: MED1 is a Mediator coactivator recruited to ER/AR-bound enhancers (its target list includes the classic estrogen-response genes GREB1, STC2, ANKRD37, plus the receptors AR, VDR, RARB, THRA themselves) and is independently documented driving ER-chromatin recruitment and RNA Pol II loading in advanced breast cancer (PMID 41092317, 41131199); NONO regulates AR/PGR-linked genes (AR, PGR, CYP17A1, KLK3) and has a documented immune-modulatory role in triple-negative breast cancer (PMID 40943463); NR2C1 cross-talks with ESR1 and RARB target genes and stemness factors (NANOG, MYC), consistent with a role tuning retinoid/estrogen signalling, though no paper in this record places it directly in breast cancer.
role_in_b: No paper or Open Targets association in this record places MED1, NONO, or NR2C1 in fibromyalgia; the fibromyalgia-labelled hits retrieved for this pair are off-target (a back-pain GWAS, an endurance-athlete cohort, a nabilone drug trial, and an incidental mention in an animal FM model), and none establish a role for this module in the disease.
shared_axis: Fibromyalgia is clinically linked to female sex and hormonal transitions (perimenopause, low testosterone), so a coactivator module that tunes ER/AR/PGR output is a mechanistically plausible bridge to breast cancer's hormone-driven biology, but that specific link is not established by anything retrieved here — it follows from the shared target-gene composition of the three factors, not from a documented finding.
reasoning: The three carrying factors independently converge on the same set of steroid-hormone-receptor genes (AR, ESR1, PGR, RARB, VDR, KLK3, CYP17A1) across their target lists, which is enough to name a real module, and MED1 is well anchored in breast cancer by three mechanistic papers; but NR2C1 has no supporting citation at all, NONO's paper concerns immune regulation rather than hormone signalling, and every fibromyalgia-side lead is off-topic, so the cross-disease connection rests on reasoning about shared hormone biology rather than on retrieved evidence.
support: PMID 41131199 (MED1 IDR deacetylation controls RNA Pol II recruitment, breast cancer); PMID 41092317 (MED1 required for ER-chromatin/CDK12 transcription complex in advanced breast cancer); PMID 41614924 (MED1 in a bulk RNA-seq breast cancer prognostic signature); PMID 40943463 (NONO regulates immune response in triple-negative breast cancer); none found for NR2C1 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In fibromyalgia patient blood or muscle samples, stratified by menopausal/androgen status, test whether MED1, NONO, and NR2C1 co-occupy the same nuclear-receptor loci (AR, ESR1, PGR, RARB, KLK3, CYP17A1) by ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN, and whether expression of those target genes tracks with FM symptom severity or hormone levels; absence of coordinated occupancy or any hormone-correlated expression signature would falsify the shared-axis claim.
caveats: Tissue pairing is asymmetric (breast tissue for the cancer network vs blood for the fibromyalgia network, likely a peripheral proxy since FM has no accessible diseased tissue), so 'shared' target agreement is read across different cell types, not the same tissue. 156 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the denominator overstates independent replication. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by blood/immune master regulators (IRF5, SPI1, PRDM1, TBX21, FLI1, CIITA), confirming the surviving factors are not simply generic blood-tissue signal; the single-view exclusion list is similarly immune-lineage TFs (STAT5B, ETS1, IKZF1, IRF4, etc.) that topped only one subgroup and are correctly absent from this account. Five of the eleven concordant factors (KLF7, YBX3 [discordant], SOX7, NR2C1 by direct citation, NAB2) have no direct literature support for either disease in this record; only MED1, NONO, and NR2C1 were judged to carry a nameable programme, and NR2C1's role rests on its target-gene composition alone, not on any citation.
